daily_brief: The most consequential development today is the confirmation of a historic trilateral summit between Presidents Trump, Xi, and Putin in China next week, where nuclear weapons reduction will be discussed [BBC], [Le Monde]. This comes as US negotiators have floated a controversial proposal for Ukraine to withdraw from Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, a significant shift in American policy that Zelensky says he would put to a referendum if security guarantees were included [BBC], [France 24]. In the Gulf, tensions escalated sharply as Bahrain accused Iran of launching repeated drone attacks on its Riffa Air Base, which hosts US military assets, with Tehran claiming it destroyed American radar installations [Al Jazeera], [Financial Times], [ABC Australia]. Domestically in the US, air travel continues to recover from Friday's four-hour nationwide ground stop—the longest since 2001—caused by a botched copper-to-fiber wire upgrade that overwhelmed legacy air traffic control systems [BBC], [Globe and Mail]. Meanwhile, at COP31 in Antalya, thousands protested environmental inaction as health experts warned of rising heat's disproportionate impact on African mothers and children [Le Monde], [RFI].

top_stories.headline: Trump, Putin, and Xi to Hold Historic Trilateral Summit in China
bullets: US President Trump, Russian President Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping will meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House confirmed
The meeting will focus on nuclear weapons reduction, which Trump has described as a priority due to proliferation concerns
Iran may also be discussed, but Ukraine is not expected to be on the agenda
No formal agreement is expected to result from the talks; this will be Trump's fourth meeting with Xi since returning to office in 2025

top_stories.headline: US Floats Ukraine Withdrawing from Donbas in Exchange for NATO Membership
bullets: Ukrainian President Zelensky revealed that US negotiators raised the possibility of Ukraine joining NATO if it withdraws remaining forces from the Donbas region
This marks the first time the US has formally raised such a territorial-for-membership exchange, according to Zelensky
Zelensky stated he would put any proposal with security guarantees, no military constraints, and reconstruction funds to a public referendum
US officials confirmed 'many ideas continue to be discussed' but said any deal must be agreed by both parties

top_stories.headline: Iran Launches Repeated Drone Attacks on US-Linked Base in Bahrain
bullets: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps launched multiple drone attacks targeting Bahrain's Riffa Air Base, which hosts US military facilities
Bahrain's military claims it intercepted several aerial attacks; Iran claims it destroyed a US early warning radar system
Bahrain condemned the attacks as violations of international law and accused Iran of using its territory to settle accounts with the United States
The US military has not confirmed Iran's claims of successful strikes; tensions follow months of relative calm in the Gulf

top_stories.headline: US Air Travel Struggles to Recover After Longest Ground Stop in 25 Years
bullets: A nationwide ground stop lasting over four hours on Friday caused approximately 12,000 flight cancellations, the longest such stoppage since the September 11, 2001 attacks
The cause was identified as a copper-to-fiber optic cable upgrade by contractor L3Harris that overloaded legacy air traffic control systems
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said officials are investigating whether contractor incompetence or faulty equipment was responsible
FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said full recovery is expected by end of Sunday, with up to 5,000 additional cancellations on Saturday

top_stories.headline: Israel Kills Senior Hamas Commander Who Helped Plan October 7 Attack
bullets: Samir Abu Younis, newly appointed commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade, was killed in an Israeli airstrike in Al-Mawasi, southern Gaza
The IDF described Younis as a central figure who participated in planning and overseeing the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel
Four missiles struck a tent in the Al-Waha camp sheltering displaced people; three injured and one dead body were transported to Nasser Hospital
Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades confirmed Younis's death, stating he had participated in numerous high-profile operations
